components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: How water moves between the ocean, the air, and the land

components.label: DEPTH 1
components.title: Evaporation
components.body: The Sun heats water in oceans, lakes, and rivers. The water turns into vapor and rises into the air, leaving most salt and impurities behind.

components.label: DEPTH 2
components.title: Condensation and Precipitation
components.body: As water vapor rises it cools and condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds. When the droplets grow heavy enough, they fall as rain, snow, sleet, or hail.

components.label: DEPTH 3
components.title: Collection and Runoff
components.body: Precipitation collects in oceans, lakes, and underground aquifers. Some water soaks into the soil, some runs off across the land into streams, and plants release water vapor through transpiration.

components.label: WORKED EXAMPLE
components.title: Tracing One Raindrop
components.body:
1. Evaporation: sunlight lifts water from the Pacific Ocean into the air.

2. Transport: winds carry the vapor inland over a mountain range.

3. Condensation: the vapor cools and forms a cloud.

4. Precipitation: the droplet falls as snow on the mountain peak.

5. Runoff: meltwater flows downhill into a river and returns to the ocean.
components.takeaway: The same water molecules keep cycling through every stage.

questions.question: What process turns liquid water into water vapor?
questions.explanation: Evaporation happens when the Sun heats liquid water and it becomes vapor.

questions.question: What happens when water vapor cools and forms clouds?
questions.explanation: Condensation turns vapor into tiny droplets that make up clouds.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a form of precipitation?
questions.explanation: Evaporation is a stage of the cycle where water becomes vapor. Rain, snow, and hail all fall from clouds.
